page: Amazon Web Services m5zn.12xlarge is an x86_64 general purpose cloud server powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8252C processors capable of reaching up to 4.5 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro System, the instance provides 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory consists of 192.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, delivering a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local NVMe storage, relying entirely on network-attached EBS volumes for persistence alongside a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Benchmark evaluations reflect solid compute throughput with pronounced strength in memory throughput and instruction execution. In raw throughput, uncached read-only memory bandwidth reached 232.82 GB/sec and write bandwidth reached 97.66 GB/sec, placing in the top 25% of measured systems alongside a PassMark memory score of 2970.07. CPU tests demonstrate reliable performance, with a single-core Geekbench score of 1567.0, a multi-core score of 13304.0, and 48931.14 on PassMark. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 31.93 GB/sec and Clang compilation scored 39054.0, both placing in the top quartile.

Performance tradeoffs center around the absence of dedicated hardware accelerators and bundled local disks. While LLM prompt processing shows moderate throughput, text generation tasks fall into the lower quartile, such as 7.75 tokens/sec on 7B parameter models, indicating that large language model inference is constrained by CPU-only execution. However, with 100 Gbps network connectivity and balanced compute-to-memory ratios, m5zn.12xlarge provides resource efficiency for software build systems, static web distribution, Redis in-memory caching, and network-intensive enterprise application workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services m5zn.12xlarge is a general purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by 48 vCPUs from a 24-core Intel Xeon 8252C processor clocked up to 4.5 GHz. The x86_64 instance provides 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory configuration. It includes no bundled local storage and no GPUs, relying on remote EBS storage and offering a high baseline network throughput of 100 Gbps. Benchmark results demonstrate strong uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 232 GB/sec read and 97 GB/sec write, along with top-quartile performance in Clang software compilation and single-threaded gzip compression. Although unaccelerated CPU-based LLM generation speeds show expected limitations, the high-frequency processor and large network pipe make the instance effective for distributed CI/CD pipelines, in-memory caching, and network-intensive enterprise workloads.
